title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized filters (filter, get, icontains). The user-supplied 'query' parameter is passed through Django's ORM query builder which handles escaping. No raw SQL or string interpolation into SQL is present.

The GlobalSearchView checks permission for documents and some object types, but the SearchResultSerializer (moved to serialisers.py) no longer extends PassUserMixin and fetches documents directly by ID using Document.objects.get(id=instance['id']) without any ownership/permission check. If a search result ID somehow references a document the user cannot view, the serializer will still return it. Additionally, the search results include users, groups, mail accounts, and mail rules — but the diff is truncated so we cannot confirm whether those queries are properly guarded. The SavedView query only filters by owner but doesn't check via get_objects_for_user_owner_aware consistently with other objects. The missing PassUserMixin on SearchResultSerializer compared to the old code (which had it) is a regression that could bypass per-object access control.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-add PassUserMixin to SearchResultSerializer or ensure the serializer context includes the request user and that per-object ownership/visibility is verified before returning document data. Also confirm that all object types returned by GlobalSearchView (users, groups, mail accounts, mail rules) are gated by appropriate permission checks.
